question: Under Section 15-10 of the Illinois Real Estate License Act of 2000, absent a written agreement between the sponsoring broker and the consumer providing for a different relationship, a licensee working with a consumer is considered to be representing that consumer as what type of agent?
explanation: Sec. 15-10 states licensees are considered to be representing the consumer they are working with as a designated agent for the consumer unless there is a written agreement providing for a different relationship.
source_note: Sec. 15-10, Relationships between licensees and consumers (225 ILCS 454/15-10)

question: Under the duties of licensees representing clients, a licensee must timely present all offers to and from the client EXCEPT when:
choice_a: the offer is below the listing price
choice_b: the client has waived this duty
choice_c: the offer comes from an unrepresented buyer
explanation: Sec. 15-15(a)(2)(B) requires timely presenting all offers to and from the client, unless the client has waived this duty.
source_note: Sec. 15-15(a)(2)(B), Duties of licensees representing clients

question: Per Sec. 15-15, a licensee representing a client must disclose to the client material facts concerning the transaction of which the licensee has actual knowledge, unless:
choice_a: the client has not specifically asked
choice_c: the material fact is unfavorable to the client
choice_d: disclosure would violate the listing agreement's marketing terms
explanation: Sec. 15-15(a)(2)(C) requires disclosing to the client material facts concerning the transaction of which the licensee has actual knowledge, unless that information is confidential information.
source_note: Sec. 15-15(a)(2)(C), Duties of licensees representing clients

question: Under Sec. 15-15(a)(2)(C), 'material facts' do NOT include which of the following, when located on or related to real estate that is not the subject of the transaction?
choice_a: Latent defects in the subject property itself
choice_b: Physical conditions that do not have a substantial adverse effect on the value of the real estate
choice_c: The seller's stated motivation for selling
explanation: The statute excludes, for real estate not the subject of the transaction: (i) physical conditions that do not have a substantial adverse effect on the value of the real estate, (ii) fact situations, and (iii) occurrences and acts at the property.
source_note: Sec. 15-15(a)(2)(C), Duties of licensees representing clients (material facts exclusion)

question: Which of the following correctly describes a duty imposed on licensees representing clients under Sec. 15-15(a)(2)(F)?
choice_a: Promote the client's best interest as opposed to the licensee's or any other person's self-interest
choice_b: Promote the sponsoring broker's business interests above the client's
choice_c: Maximize the licensee's own compensation from the transaction
choice_d: Prioritize the interests of cooperating brokers in the transaction
explanation: Sec. 15-15(a)(2)(F) requires acting in a manner consistent with promoting the client's best interests as opposed to a licensee's or any other person's self-interest.
source_note: Sec. 15-15(a)(2)(F), Duties of licensees representing clients

question: When a licensee is preparing or making contemporaneous offers or contracts to purchase or lease the same property on behalf of multiple clients, Sec. 15-15(b) requires the licensee to:
choice_a: decline to represent any of the clients involved
choice_b: obtain only oral consent from each client before proceeding
choice_c: provide written disclosure to all such clients and refer to another designated agent any client who requests such a referral
choice_d: represent only the client whose offer is highest
explanation: Sec. 15-15(b) requires a licensee to provide written disclosure to all clients for whom the licensee is preparing or making contemporaneous offers or contracts to purchase or lease the same property, and to refer to another designated agent any client that requests such referral.
source_note: Sec. 15-15(b), Duties of licensees representing clients (contemporaneous offers)

question: A licensee representing a buyer or tenant client who works on the basis of receiving a higher fee or compensation based on a higher selling price or lease cost:
choice_a: automatically breaches the licensee's fiduciary duty to the client
choice_b: will not be presumed to have breached a duty or obligation to that client
choice_c: must reduce the fee to a standard, fixed rate
choice_d: must disclose this arrangement in a separate signed addendum before every showing
explanation: Sec. 15-15(c) provides that a licensee representing a buyer or tenant client will not be presumed to have breached a duty or obligation to that client by working on the basis of receiving a higher fee tied to a higher selling price or lease cost.
source_note: Sec. 15-15(c), Duties of licensees representing clients

question: Under Sec. 15-15(d), a licensee shall not be liable to a client for providing false information to the client if that information was provided to the licensee by a customer, UNLESS:
choice_a: the client specifically requested that the information be verified
choice_b: the false information related to the purchase price
choice_c: the licensee knew or should have known the information was false
choice_d: the customer providing the information was unrepresented
explanation: Sec. 15-15(d) states a licensee shall not be liable to a client for providing false information from a customer unless the licensee knew or should have known the information was false.
source_note: Sec. 15-15(d), Duties of licensees representing clients

question: Under Sec. 15-25, a licensee engaged by a seller client must timely disclose to prospective buyer customers which category of facts?
choice_a: All facts known to the seller, whether or not communicated to the licensee
choice_b: Latent material adverse facts pertaining to the physical condition of the property that are actually known by the licensee and could not be discovered by a reasonably diligent inspection by the customer
choice_c: The complete pricing history of comparable listings
choice_d: Any information requested by the buyer's attorney regardless of the licensee's knowledge
explanation: Sec. 15-25 requires a licensee engaged by a seller client to timely disclose to prospective buyer customers all latent material adverse facts pertaining to the physical condition of the property that are actually known by the licensee and that could not be discovered by a reasonably diligent inspection of the property by the customer.

question: Per Sec. 15-25, what protection is afforded to a licensee for revealing information in compliance with that Section?
choice_a: Immunity from all Department of Financial and Professional Regulation discipline
choice_b: No cause of action shall arise on behalf of any person against the licensee for revealing that information
choice_c: A statutory defense limited to breach-of-contract claims
choice_d: Automatic indemnification by the sponsoring broker
explanation: Sec. 15-25 states no cause of action shall arise on behalf of any person against a licensee for revealing information in compliance with this Section.

question: Under Sec. 15-35(a), a licensee acting as a designated agent must advise a consumer in writing of the designated agency relationship no later than:
choice_b: beginning to work as a designated agent on behalf of the consumer
choice_c: 3 business days after the property is listed
choice_d: the preparation of an offer to purchase or lease
explanation: Sec. 15-35(a) requires a licensee acting as a designated agent to advise a consumer in writing, no later than beginning to work as a designated agent on behalf of the consumer, that a designated agency relationship exists (unless otherwise agreed) and the name(s) of the designated agent(s).

question: Sec. 15-35(b) requires the licensee representing the consumer to discuss with the consumer:
choice_a: the licensee's personal tax obligations related to the sale
choice_b: the sponsoring broker's compensation policy, including the terms of compensation and any amounts offered to cooperating brokers who represent other parties in a transaction
choice_d: a list of competing brokerages in the market area
explanation: Sec. 15-35(b) requires the licensee representing the consumer to discuss with the consumer the sponsoring broker's compensation policy, including the terms of compensation and any amounts offered to cooperating brokers who represent other parties in a transaction.

question: Under Sec. 15-35(c), a licensee must disclose in writing to a customer that the licensee is not acting as the customer's agent, at a time intended to prevent disclosure of confidential information, but in no event later than:
choice_a: the first showing of the property
choice_b: the signing of the listing agreement
choice_c: the preparation of an offer to purchase or lease real property
explanation: Sec. 15-35(c) requires the written non-agency disclosure to a customer to be made at a time intended to prevent disclosure of confidential information, but in no event later than the preparation of an offer to purchase or lease real property.

question: According to Sec. 15-40, the payment or promise of payment of compensation to a licensee:
choice_a: automatically creates an agency relationship with the payor
choice_b: is not determinative of whether an agency relationship has been created between any licensee and a consumer
choice_c: must be disclosed to IDFPR within 24 hours
choice_d: voids any prior designated agency agreement
explanation: Sec. 15-40 states that compensation does not determine agency: the payment or promise of payment of compensation to a licensee is not determinative of whether an agency relationship has been created between any licensee and a consumer.
source_note: Sec. 15-40, Compensation does not determine agency

question: Under Sec. 15-45(a), an individual licensee (or the sponsored licensees a sponsoring broker permits) may act as a dual agent in the same transaction only with:
choice_a: the verbal consent of the sponsoring broker
choice_b: the informed written consent of all clients
choice_c: prior approval from the Department of Financial and Professional Regulation
choice_d: the consent of the buyer client only
explanation: Sec. 15-45(a) provides that a licensee may act as a dual agent, or a sponsoring broker may permit sponsored licensees to act as dual agents in the same transaction, only with the informed written consent of all clients.

question: Under Sec. 15-45(c), when should a licensee acting in a dual agency capacity obtain written confirmation from clients of their prior consent to dual agency?
choice_a: At the initial listing appointment, before any offers exist
choice_b: At the time the clients are executing any offer or contract to purchase or lease in the transaction
choice_d: Only if a dispute later arises between the clients
explanation: Sec. 15-45(c) requires the confirmation to be obtained at the time the clients are executing any offer or contract to purchase or lease in a transaction in which the licensee is acting as a dual agent.

question: Under Sec. 15-45(g), a licensee shall NOT serve as a dual agent in a transaction when:
choice_a: the transaction is a lease rather than a sale
choice_b: the licensee has held a license for less than one year
choice_c: the licensee, or an entity in which the licensee has or will have any ownership interest, is a party to the transaction
choice_d: compensation is split unevenly between the two clients
explanation: Sec. 15-45(g) states a licensee shall not serve as a dual agent in any transaction when the licensee, or an entity in which the licensee has or will have any ownership interest, is a party to the transaction.

question: Under Sec. 10-10(a), a licensee must disclose to a client the sponsoring broker's compensation policy, including:
choice_b: the terms of compensation and any amounts offered to cooperating brokers who represent other parties in a transaction
choice_d: the commission split among every agent in the office
explanation: Sec. 10-10(a) requires a licensee to disclose to a client the sponsoring broker's compensation policy, including the terms of compensation and any amounts offered to cooperating brokers who represent other parties in a transaction.

question: Under Sec. 10-10(c), if a licensee refers a client to a third party (other than a publicly held or traded company) for services related to the transaction, and the licensee has greater than what ownership interest in that third party, must the licensee disclose that fact to the client at the time of making the referral?
explanation: Sec. 10-10(c) requires disclosure when the licensee has greater than a 1% ownership interest in the third party (or receives or may receive dividends or other profit sharing distributions from it), other than a publicly held or traded company.

question: Under Sec. 10-27, each licensee must disclose, in writing, his or her status as a licensee to all parties in a transaction when:
choice_a: the licensee refers a family member as a client
choice_b: the licensee is selling, leasing, or purchasing any interest, direct or indirect, in the real estate that is the subject of the transaction
choice_c: the licensee has held a license for fewer than two years
choice_d: the transaction involves commercial property exclusively
explanation: Sec. 10-27 requires each licensee to disclose, in writing, his or her status as a licensee to all parties in a transaction when the licensee is selling, leasing, or purchasing any interest, direct or indirect, in the real estate that is the subject of the transaction.
